title: Hegseth says 20% of senior military officers will be cut, unveils new AI command
key_facts: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gave a 'State of the Force' address at Marine Corps base Quantico, Virginia, on Wednesday to about 600 service members, unveiling six new initiatives.
One is AUTOWARCOM, a four-star Autonomous Warfighting Command to integrate fast-developing autonomous drone technology and AI.

Hegseth confirmed that 20% of general and flag officer slots will go: he said 10% of generals and admirals were fired and the number of slots is cut by a further 10%; there are 841 active-duty generals and admirals.
He also announced an Office of Religious Affairs with a direct line to the secretary, and a 'Project Meridien' study of future warfare involving Elon Musk, Newt Gingrich and Anduril's Palmer Luckey.
He said the US will build a new base for the first time in 40 years and that every major installation will generate its own power independent of the civilian grid.
ABC says the cuts follow a broader purge of senior officers whose rationale Hegseth has not publicly explained.
Hegseth criticised DEI programmes and journalists in the speech, calling some reporting 'treason'.
quote_evidence: Hegseth also announced the creation of AUTOWARCOM, which stands for Autonomous Warfighting Command, to integrate fast-developing autonomous drone technologies and artificial intelligence.
The media calls that a purge; I call that accountability and long overdue.
There are currently 841 active-duty generals and admirals, according to Defense Department data.
why_it_matters_hint: The US military is creating a four-star command for autonomous weapons and AI while shrinking its top officer ranks.
event_date: Speech on Wednesday 30 Sep 2026 (inferred from earlier coverage); item dated 10 Oct 2026.
